title: Turn-based RPG Combat System
author: irbrandonl
selftext:
Hey y'all!Back with another development update for GODSCAR, my dark fantasy turn-based RPG!

This time, I wanted to give you guys a closer look at something I've been putting a lot of work into: the battle system!

GodScar takes inspiration from classic turn-based RPGs like Final Fantasy and Octopath Traveler, but I'm trying to bring my own spin to the formula.

One of my biggest goals is to make combat feel strategic, challenging, and visually satisfying, where every decision matters and you can't just rely on spamming your strongest abilities to win.

A few things I'm working on include...

 Strategic turn-based combat — Different jobs, abilities, enemy mechanics, and tactical decisions that encourage players to approach encounters in different ways.

Divine Powers — Borrow strength from powerful gods, each with their own unique abilities, mechanics, and resources. I want divine abilities to feel genuinely extraordinary compared to ordinary attacks.

Massive 3D Colossal Bosses — Fully animated 3D creatures integrated into the game's HD-2D visual style, with powerful attacks, unique mechanics, and environmental interactions.

 Armor Break and Stagger Mechanics — Battles that reward understanding your enemies, exploiting openings, breaking defenses, and knowing when to attack or defend.

Different Jobs and Playstyles — A variety of character classes, each offering its own approach to combat, with additional jobs and abilities to discover throughout the game.

Dynamic Battlefield Effects — Weather conditions, environmental hazards, and other mechanics designed to make encounters feel more unpredictable and immersive.

Looking back at this footage, I can already spot quite a few things I want to improve, especially when it comes to animations, visual effects, combat presentation, and overall polish. But that's part of the development process, and I wanted to share where things currently stand rather than waiting until everything is perfect.

I'd really love to hear what you guys think! What stands out to you? What would you change or improve? Does the combat look engaging, or is there something you feel is missing?

Constructive criticism is always welcome! A lot of the feedback I've received from previous posts has already helped me improve GODSCAR, so I genuinely appreciate everyone taking the time to share their thoughts.

And if you're curious about my development workflow, feel free to ask! I'm always happy to share more about how I'm building everything.

Developed using Claude Opus 5.5 (Extra Effort) • Blender • Godot

comments.author: Braunb8888
comments.body: Looks good man, but the characters seem to be paper cutouts, compared to the enemies it looks weird. Add some 3D depth to them and it’ll match better. Visuals are pretty as hell. Im working on a jrpg too but its muddy, dark, ps1 style by comparison.

replies.author: irbrandonl
replies.body: Thank you! Got suggestions on how to do that?The sprites themselves are 2d and Im going for 2.5D visuals similar to Octopath Traveler. Most of the monsters are 2d with the exception of some collosal monsters in the game that are 3d. Right now there are probably about 7 bosses that are 3d amongst the 100+ monsters. So a very small margin. I was thinking maybe just going all out 2d for sprites including collosal monsters but not sure yet.. still needing feedback. Thanks again!

replies.author: Braunb8888
replies.body: Yes, tell Claude what you’re looking to do, and be detailed, say you want 3D depth to your 2d characters. Send examples and see what pops out.
